changes.comment: BREAKING: IMemoryStore.put / delete take an optional { expected } precondition (the record's seq, or 'absent' for put), checked under the write lock before dedup, and return MemoryWriteResult<T> — a DetailedResult carrying a classified IMemoryWriteFailure (conflict / duplicate / invalid / rejected / not-found / io); a caller that chains a plain-Result continuation onto put / delete adds .asResult. Under expected, a put whose content already exists under another id fails 'duplicate' instead of returning that record. FileTreeMemoryStore persists a seq high-water mark in two alternating root files (memory-store.seq.a.json / .b.json) so a seq is never re-issued across a restart; seq stays strictly increasing but is no longer dense. A flat put now reads its same-id record before content dedup, so an unreadable same-id file fails the put even when a cross-id duplicate exists. Ingest merge-into writes under the snapshot seq and reports a moved target as disposition 'conflict', and a duplicate as 'deduped'.
